name: Shao's three units theorem: density 5/8 forces a three-fold additive basis
description:
Let $m$ be an odd squarefree positive integer and let $A$ be a set of units modulo $m$ with $|A| > \frac{5}{8}\varphi(m)$. Then $A + A + A = \mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$, so every residue class, unit or not, is a sum of three elements of $A$.

This is Corollary 1.5 of Xuancheng Shao, *A density version of the Vinogradov three primes theorem*, Duke Math. J. 163 (2014) 489-512, [arXiv:1206.6139v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.6139). It's the local input to Shao's density version of the three primes theorem.

## Sharpness

At $m = 15$ the set $\{2, 8, 11, 13, 14\}$ holds five of the eight units, so $|A| = \frac{5}{8}\varphi(15)$ exactly. And 1 is not a sum of three of its elements. That's equality in the hypothesis, and the conclusion already fails, so $<$ can't be weakened to $\le$.

## Where the proof comes from

Induction on sets fails, because passing from $m$ to a prime factor $p$ splits $A$ into fibers of different densities. A set is too rigid to carry through that split. Functions $f : \mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z} \to [0,1]$ aren't, so Shao proves a weighted statement, Proposition 1.4, and the corollary is its case $f = 1_A$.

The weighted statement then splits at the primes 3 and 5. For $m$ coprime to 30 the induction runs on prime factors, using Cauchy-Davenport-Chowla for three sets. It gives the stronger pairwise-product conclusion $f(a)f(b) + f(b)f(c) + f(c)f(a) > \frac{5}{8}(f(a) + f(b) + f(c))$. Modulo 15, Shao solves a linear program over the eight units instead. Two averaging inequalities, one symmetric and one asymmetric, turn a density above $5/8$ into a single good triple. The milestones follow Shao's numbering.

## Formalization

We state every item in Mathlib primitives (`IsUnit`, `Nat.totient`, `Odd`, `Squarefree`, `Finset`, and `Antitone`), so the mission doesn't need definition items. We write the units modulo $m$ as `Finset.univ.filter (fun x => IsUnit x)` at each use instead of naming them, so an auditor only has to trust Mathlib.

We write $|A| > \frac{5}{8}\varphi(m)$ as `5 * Nat.totient m < 8 * A.card`, which keeps the goal in $\mathbb{N}$.
